cards.text: Meet Zephaniah, a prophet in the days of Josiah, king of Judah (Zephaniah 1:1). He just finished warning that the great Day of the LORD is near, near and coming quickly (Zephaniah 1:14). Now he calls out, “Gather yourselves, gather together, O shameful nation,” and then he gives a reason to hurry.

cards.question: Zephaniah tells the shameful nation to gather together. What does he want them to gather before?

answers.text: The Day of the LORD's anger

cards.text: Three times in one verse he says “before”: before the decree takes effect, before the burning anger of the LORD, before the Day of the LORD's anger. Friend, that's not a gentle reminder, that's an oven timer going BEEP BEEP BEEP.
Then the prophet turns to all the humble of the earth, the ones who carry out His justice.

cards.question: What does Zephaniah tell all the humble of the earth to do?
Zephaniah promises the humble they will surely be sheltered on the day of the LORD's anger.

cards.text: He tells them to seek righteousness and seek humility, and says, “Perhaps you will be sheltered on the day of the LORD's anger.” Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer hoping somebody would come looking for tape, so a perhaps from the LORD? I'll TAKE it.
Then Zephaniah says “For,” and names four cities: Gaza, Ashkelon, Ashdod and Ekron.

cards.question: Gaza will be ___, and Ashkelon left in ruins.

cards.text: Ashdod will be driven out at noon, and Ekron will be uprooted. NOON, friend, no sneaking out at midnight, they get driven out in broad daylight.
Then comes a “Woe” for the dwellers of the seacoast, the nation of the Cherethites, and the word of the LORD is against Canaan.

cards.question: The word of the LORD is against Canaan on the seacoast. Whose land is it?

cards.text: Then the LORD says, “I will destroy you, and no one will be left.” So what happens to a coastline with nobody on it?

cards.question: The emptied seacoast becomes a land of pastures, with wells for shepherds and folds for sheep.
Zephaniah says the coast will end up belonging to someone. Who?
The remnant of Judah will lie down in the evening among the houses of Ashkelon.
The remnant of Judah can rest among the houses of Ashkelon, for the LORD their God will attend to them and ___ their captives.

cards.text: Now the LORD speaks about Moab and the Ammonites, two nations that came from Lot's sons (Genesis 19:37-38). He says, “I have heard the reproach of Moab and the insults of the Ammonites,” and then He says what they did.

cards.question: What did Moab and the Ammonites do to the LORD's people?

answers.text: Taunted them and threatened their borders
Traded with them and shared their land
Fled from them and left their towns

cards.text: Then the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says, “as surely as I live,” and He compares these two nations to two famous cities.

cards.question: Moab will be like ___ and the Ammonites like ___.

cards.text: He says they'll be “a place of weeds and salt pits, a perpetual wasteland.” Perpetual, friend, that's not a fixer-upper, that's a FOR SALE sign nobody EVER takes down.

cards.question: The LORD says the remnant of His people will plunder Moab and the Ammonites.
Zephaniah says Moab and the Ammonites get all this in return for something. What?

cards.text: The LORD will be terrifying to them when He starves all the gods of the earth. Every one of those gods is about to find out what the back of a junk drawer feels like, and trust me, I've got the dust to prove it.

cards.question: Then the nations of every shore will ___ Him, each in its own place.

cards.text: Next comes one short line for the Cushites, the people of Cush, the land past Egypt's southern border (Ezekiel 29:10): “You too, O Cushites, will be slain by My sword.” Then the LORD will stretch out His hand against the north.

cards.question: The LORD stretches out His hand against the north. Which nation will He destroy?

cards.text: And He goes after Nineveh, a city built long ago in Assyria (Genesis 10:11). Yes, THAT Nineveh, the one Jonah tried so hard not to visit (Jonah 1:2-3).

cards.question: The LORD will make Nineveh a desolation, as dry as a desert.
Once Nineveh is a dry desolation, who moves in?

cards.text: Owls roost atop her pillars, and their calls sound from the window. That's not a city anymore, friend, that's a nature documentary where the narrator is whispering.
Desolation lies on the threshold, for He will expose the beams of cedar. Nobody's answering that door.
Then Zephaniah calls Nineveh “This carefree city that dwells securely.” You know that friend who leaves the oven on, walks out the door and says, “Relax, it's FINE”? Yeah.

cards.question: What does Nineveh, the carefree city, think to herself?

answers.text: That no one else compares to her

cards.question: People passing by ruined Nineveh stop to weep for her.

cards.text: Instead everyone who passes by her hisses and shakes his fist, and the city that thought to herself, “I am it,” is a resting place for beasts. Friend, that's every cookie that ever bragged it couldn't burn.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 17 quotes "This carefree city that dwells securely.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: the statement about seeking and shelter, the junk-drawer question, and “I'll TAKE it.”

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The setup only says that the LORD compares the nations to two famous cities. It gives no sufficient basis for reasoning out Sodom and Gomorrah, or which name belongs in which blank, rather than recalling wording that has not yet been shown.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
